newsitem.title: USA: M.A. Hanna finalizing deal with Harwick.
newsitem.headline: M.A. Hanna finalizing deal with Harwick.

text.p: M.A. Hanna Co, an international specialty chemicals company, said Thursday it was finalizing negotiations to acquire the manufacturing business of Harwick Chemical Corp.
Hanna said that the acquisition includes Harwick's manufacturing divisions, Republic Chemical Co, based in Akron, Ohio, and CMS Chemical Co, based in Wynne, Ark.
Harwick's distribution business is not included in the transaction, it said.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Hanna will operate Harwick's manufacturing business, which had sales of about $60 million in 1996, as a separate unit under the name Harwick Chemical Manufacturing Corp. It said Harwick's headquarters in Akron is not included in the sale.
Harwick will continue to supply product under a two-year agreement while M.A. Hanna relocates the Akron operations to a new facility, Hanna said.

Harwick's manufacturing division employs about 300, and supplies chemical dispersions, specialty colorants and other specialty products for the rubber industry, and specialty color pigment dispersions and dry colorants for plastics.
The acquisition is subject to governmental and other approvals and is expected to be completed in early September, Hanna said.

"The addition of the Harwick business will allow us to broaden our product offerings and expand our overall capabilities in the rubber industry," said Douglas J. McGregor, Hanna's chairman and chief executive officer.

Gene Corbett, Harwick president and CEO, said the transaction was in the best interest of the company's customers, employees and shareholders and will allow it to return to its roots as a distribution company.
Harwick will change to its name to Harwick Standard Distribution Corp to reflect that focus, he said.
